From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@auroraapps.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning & capacity increase (40 -> 80 GPUs)

Hi Aditya,

We're kicking off our renewal conversation for Q2 and want to lock in an expanded reserved pool. Current contract has 40 GPUs reserved; we expect to double that to 80 for CY27 due to an upcoming Gen-2 multimodal rollout. Primary asks:

- Reserved pool increase to 80 GPUs, committed for 12 months.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained X tokens/sec baseline for our inference traffic (I'll share metrics separately).
- SLA question: because the migration and stateful model warming will be disruptive, we're asking Redwood for a temporary SLA grace period (no uptime credits or latency penalties) for a bounded migration window. Specifically, we'd like a 30–45 day tolerance window after the new pool goes live while you help warm caches and tune batching.

We understand this is non-standard; before we sign the renewal we want the terms and any trade-offs documented (latency p95 targets, credit formula, rollback triggers). Also attaching a rough traffic forecast and launch timeline.

Can you put together an outline of how Redwood would approach the expand+migration and what SLA exceptions you would be willing to allow? We plan to get legal and infra involved on our end once we have your ask/offer.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
VP of Infrastructure
Aurora Apps, Inc.

Hi Sanjay,

Really appreciate the clear ask and the forecast — this is the sort of signal we need to plan capacity. High-level response below and then I'll loop in our Solutions and Legal teams for the fine print.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Contract: 12-month reserved commitment for 80 GPUs (term pricing attached).
- Migration: staged onboarding over 2 weeks of rolling model placements + 2 weeks of warm-up, followed by a 30-day stabilization period.
- SLA grace period request: we can support a "grace period" during the stabilization window where latency SLOs are relaxed to the documented migration SLOs and uptime credits are suspended, provided both sides agree to a runbook and success criteria. We typically negotiate a defined window (30–45 days) and explicit rollback triggers.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll attach a draft pricing page and a migration runbook.
2) Loop in Marissa (Solutions) to review the technical warm-up plan.
3) Loop in Rishi (Legal) to draft an SLA addendum with the grace period language and the credit formula.

If that direction sounds good, I'll schedule a short sync early next week to align timelines.

Best,

Aditya / team — reviewed their forecast and sketched a technical approach. Highlights: 

- Pre-warm strategy: allocate an initial subset (20 GPUs) in a staging pool to run live shadow traffic + background prefix caching for 7–10 days before promoting to production.
- Autoscale & batching: recommend temporarily increasing batch windows by 25% during the first 2 weeks post-cutover to reduce tail latency variance while warm caches populate. We'll monitor p95/p99 closely.
- KV/prefix caching: some of Aurora's models are sensitive to cold KV cache misses; we'll prioritize hot model shards first and stagger cold start models.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive hours OR error rates above 2% will trigger immediate rollback & communication plan.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: Contract signed + PO
- Week 1: Staging pool + shadowing (20 GPUs)
- Week 2: Promote subset to prod, ramp to 50% traffic
- Week 3–4: Full promotion to 80 GPUs, accelerated warm-up
- Day 30–45: Stabilization window ends; final tuning and SLA reassessment

Attachments: migration_runbook.md (runbook draft with detailed steps, monitoring dashboards, and rollback playbook).

I'll be on the Aurora call next Wed and can walk through the runbook. From an ops POV, a 45-day stabilization window is reasonable; we should avoid an open-ended exception.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team — quick legal/contract note for the Aurora renewal:

1) SLA addendum: draft language attached (sla_addendum_draft.docx). Proposal: define a bounded "SLA grace period" equal to the stabilization window (max 45 days) during which latency SLOs will be replaced by migration SLOs documented in the runbook and uptime credits are suspended.
2) Credit formula: if post-stabilization p95 exceeds agreed target, credits will accrue from day 46 onward per the standard credit schedule; no credits will be paid for the grace period unless there is gross negligence in execution.
3) Rollback & termination: include explicit rollback triggers (Marissa's ops triggers) and a mutual termination clause if performance cannot be restored within 7 business days after a rollback event.

I'll circulate a tracked-change addendum for Aditya to send to Aurora. We should also capture the PO/acceptance timeline in HubSpot and request a signed DocuSign for the addendum before we start the production promotion.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
